title: The RAG dual-channel panorama: indexing (offline, once) and open-book querying (every question)

events.label: Indexing · gather the knowledge-base documents
events.detail: 120 internal documents (PDF / web exports / Markdown), about 480k tokens in total, covering policies, product manuals, and support-ticket archives (numbers are illustrative teaching data). Before indexing, clean them: strip headers and footers, convert tables to text, and keep the heading hierarchy.

events.label: Indexing · chunk (512/64)
events.detail: About 512 tokens per chunk with a 64-token overlap between neighbors: 480k tokens yield roughly 1,070 chunks. The overlap keeps a sentence or semantic unit from being cut exactly at a boundary — cross-boundary information survives in both neighboring chunks.

events.label: Indexing · send 1,070 chunks to embedding in batches
events.detail: Call the embedding API in batches (64 chunks per batch): batching collapses network round trips, so indexing throughput is far higher than one-request-per-chunk.

events.label: Indexing · batch embedding → 1536-dim vectors
events.detail: Each text chunk is encoded into a 1536-dimension floating-point vector: the closer the meaning, the smaller the angle between vectors. Once chosen, the embedding model is frozen. At $0.02 per 1M tokens, 480k tokens cost about $0.01 (illustrative) — indexing is a one-time investment.

events.label: Indexing · store vector + original text + metadata
events.detail: A record stores three things: the vector (for retrieval), the original text (this is what ultimately goes into the prompt), and metadata (document name / section / date, for filtering and citation).

events.label: Indexing · index ready (offline stage ends)
events.detail: The 1,070 vectors become a searchable index keyed by cosine similarity (ANN-accelerated). This stage reruns only when the knowledge base changes and has nothing to do with user questions — a compile-time artifact that the runtime reuses directly.

events.label: Open-book · ask a question
events.detail: 「What is the Q3 payment-collection policy?」— the training corpus contains no internal policy for this company; asking the model directly only yields fabrication or outdated generalities.

events.label: POST /ask (with the question)
events.detail: The query stage begins. Unlike the indexing stage, this pipeline runs in full on every single question.

events.label: Open-book · embed the query with the same model
events.detail: Iron rule: the query must be embedded with exactly the same model used at indexing time. Different models have incompatible vector spaces; mixing them distorts similarity and collapses retrieval quality.

events.label: Query vector returned (1536-dim)
events.detail: Only one sentence is embedded, taking about 20 ms. Next: find the few nearest document vectors among the 1,070.

events.label: Open-book · cosine-similarity retrieval, top-5
events.detail: Compute cosine similarity against every document vector and take the top 5; in this example the scores are 0.91 / 0.88 / 0.85 / 0.71 / 0.42 (illustrative). The fifth is already weakly relevant — bigger k is not better: low-scoring chunks dilute the context and crowd the window.

events.label: Top-5 original chunks and metadata returned
events.detail: The original text and metadata stored at indexing time come back together — that is the only way an answer can cite 「which document, which section」.

events.label: Open-book · assemble the augmented prompt
events.detail: A system note instructing 「answer only from the material below; if you cannot cite a source, say so」 + the 5 retrieved passages + the user's question. Open-book means putting the exam paper (the material) into the model's hands.

events.label: POST /chat/completions (augmented prompt)
events.detail: Identical call protocol to E01's ordinary request; everything different lives in the request body: messages now include the retrieved passages, and temperature is usually lowered (e.g. 0.2) to curb unsourced improvisation.

events.label: Open-book · generate the answer from the material
events.detail: Token-by-token generation, constrained to the material, with [1][2]-style citations; when the material runs out, output 「not found in the material」 instead of fabricating — that second half must be explicitly demanded by the system prompt.

events.label: SSE streaming back
events.detail: The same SSE frame flow as E01. RAG does not change the model-calling protocol — only what gets fed into the model.

events.label: Final answer with citations
events.detail: 「Key points of the Q3 payment-collection policy… [Source: Payment Collection Rules (2026 revision) §3.2]」, with cited sources listed under the answer so users can open and verify the originals. Traceability is the open-book exam's biggest advantage over closed-book.
